100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 3, 1926, tensions escalated in Europe as the League of Nations convened to address the ongoing crises in the Ruhr region and the broader economic instability following World War I. In the United States, the stock market showed signs of volatility, raising concerns among investors about the potential for a downturn. Meanwhile, the world of entertainment buzzed with the success of "The Jazz Singer," signaling a shift in the film industry toward sound.
